label: Account Card
title: Account Card
summary: Use an Account Card for one linked account in a row of accounts, or as the tile that adds another.
corePrinciple: One account per tile, and one tile to add another.

anatomy.title: Art, a name, and a masked number
anatomy.description: A connected tile shows the account's art above its name and masked number. The add tile swaps the art for a lavender field with a plus and drops the number.

configuration.title: Connected or add
configuration.description: state picks the tile: connected shows art, a name, and a masked number; add shows a lavender field with a plus and a title, with no number. imageRatio sets the art's shape, 125 : 82 by default, and cardSlot can replace the art or the field with your own content. Modes only recolour the add tile's plus.

states.title: A preview or a button
states.description: Without onPress the tile is a preview, named by its title. onPress makes the whole tile one button that fades to 70% while pressed. disabled dims it to half and, on a pressable tile, stops presses. It has no selected state.
blocks: The whole tile is one button.

sizing.title: As wide as where you put it
sizing.description: It fills its host's width, so set the width where you place it: Figma's tiles are 125 px, as in Storybook and the Card Accounts carousel. The art keeps its ratio, with 8 px to the text, so at 125 px a connected tile is 122 px tall and an add tile 106.

content.title: A name and a mask
content.description: Title each tile with the account's name in a few words, such as “Joint account”: it's cut to one line. Show only the masked number, in the bank's own format. Title the add tile with its action, “Add account”, because its title is also what screen readers announce.

inContext.title: Linked accounts
inContext.description: The Accounts screen shows each linked account as a tile, with the add tile last. Each tile's onPress is the screen's own action: open the account, or start linking a new one. For more tiles than fit, CarouselCardAccounts scrolls them.

sources.title: Use the public Account Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (12 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Account Card is a component set with Connected and Add tiles, 125 px wide, and Title and Subtitle text. Its card art has rounded corners; the code doesn’t round the art, only the add field. The package ships no card art, so this page uses a photo, as Storybook’s From URL story does. Modes only recolour the add tile’s plus; the text and the lavender field don’t change. The tile ignores the theme provider, so pass modes on it. The published Storybook still shows the old page.
